standard.title: Rehearse and refine aesthetic choices
standard.description: rehearse and refine drama making deliberate aesthetic choices to unify dramatic meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can evaluate and refine use of elements and conventions to shape dramatic action (Y7-8). They can plan, organise and rehearse, and adjust performance based on feedback and audience response.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students rehearse and refine drama, making deliberate aesthetic choices to unify dramatic meaning.

nodes.label: Deliberate aesthetic choice-making
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the aesthetic choices operating in their drama — and articulate why each choice serves the unified dramatic meaning.
nodes.minimum_width: Student identifies at least three aesthetic choices (elements, conventions, design) in their drama and explains how each contributes to unified meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Students evaluate how ideas, emotions and audience response can be used to refine the drama; they consider the impact of design elements (costume, prop, set, lighting, sound) on meaning and aesthetic effect; they manipulate elements and use conventions to create and manipulate actor-audience relationships.
wider: Students take on specific production roles (director, designer, stage manager) and articulate aesthetic decisions from within that role
Students evaluate how actor-audience relationship conventions (fourth wall, direct address, immersive staging) change the nature of audience experience and adjust their choices accordingly
nodes.hinge_reason: The concept of aesthetic unity — all choices serving a single coherent meaning — is what distinguishes sophisticated drama-making at this band from technically competent but unfocused work; without this frame, refining is just fixing individual problems rather than shaping a unified work.

response_modes.reason: Introduce 'aesthetic unity' as an explicit concept before the refinement phase; use analysis of existing works to model what it looks like, before applying the lens to students' own drama.

success_criteria: Student identifies at least three aesthetic choices in their drama
Student explains how each choice contributes to the unified dramatic meaning — not just what it does technically, but why it belongs in this work

nodes.label: Refining through rehearsal toward unified meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use the rehearsal process to strengthen and unify dramatic action — adjusting pace, staging, vocal delivery, transitions and design toward a coherent intended effect.
nodes.minimum_width: Student makes at least two documented refinements during rehearsal in response to evaluation of how well the drama achieves its intention.
nodes.typical_width: Students focus and strengthen dramatic action by manipulating pace, cues, vocal tone, physical proximity and transitions; they collaborate as directors and performers — blocking staging, directing action; they reflect and evaluate how successfully intentions and effects were achieved, and draw lessons for future practice.
wider: Students collaborate with community members or external performers in a shared production process, managing ownership, protocol and collective decision-making about aesthetic choices
Students document and analyse their refinement process — using annotated scripts, rehearsal notes or video review — to develop metacognitive awareness of their own practice

response_modes.reason: Refinement is the integration of all prior skills and knowledge into a cohesive artistic work. Structured post-rehearsal evaluation ('Was the intention achieved? What broke the unity?') is the essential teaching scaffold.

Refining drama across different performance contexts — class showing, external audience, community collaboration — builds richer understanding of what 'unified meaning' looks like for different audiences.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Refining drama for different audiences and contexts — and with different collaborators — generates genuinely rich learning about aesthetic choice and cultural communication that cannot be achieved within a single production context.
success_criteria: Student makes at least two documented refinements during rehearsal in response to evaluation
Student can explain how each refinement strengthens the unified dramatic meaning
Student evaluates how successfully the final work achieves its intention and draws at least one lesson for future practice
